records.source: וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן־אָדָם֙ הִנָּבֵ֣א עַל־גּ֔וֹג וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ גּ֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֥שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָֽל׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
pieces: As for you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

L.1: And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and you will say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

R.1: Son of man, prophesy against Gog. Tell him, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, I am against you.

decisions.choice: the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: as in 38:2
decisions.reason: The phrase is the same as in 38:2-3. *Rosh* is taken as "chief", the head prince over Meshech and Tubal; the Septuagint and some later translations read it as a name, "the prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal". No people called Rosh is known from this period. Either way, Rosh is not Russia, whose name comes from the medieval Rus'. See 38:2.

decisions.choice: and you, son of man: the second part of the message against Gog
decisions.reason: Chapter 39 retells Gog's defeat (verses 1-8) and goes on to its aftermath: the burning of the weapons (verses 9-10), the burial (verses 11-16), the feast of the birds and beasts (verses 17-20), and the LORD's purpose for Israel and the nations (verses 21-29).

decisions.choice: the chief prince (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase at every level, as in 38:2. The formula follows 2:4.

records.heading: Gog's defeat

records.source: וְשֹׁבַבְתִּ֨יךָ֙ וְשִׁשֵּׁאתִ֔יךָ וְהַעֲלִיתִ֖יךָ מִיַּרְכְּתֵ֣י צָפ֑וֹן וַהֲבִאוֹתִ֖ךָ עַל־הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I will turn you around and drive you on and bring you up from [the] remotest parts of [the] north, and bring you against [the] mountains of Israel.
pieces: I will turn you around and drive you along. I will bring you up from the far north and lead you against the mountains of Israel.

L.2: And I will turn you around and drive you on, and bring you up from the remotest parts of the north, and bring you against the mountains of Israel.

R.2: I will turn you around and lead you. I will bring you from the far north and make you attack the mountains of Israel.

decisions.choice: drive you on: the verb is uncertain
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here. It is usually taken as "lead along" or "drive on"; the Septuagint reads "guide". The point is the same as the hooks of 38:4: the LORD leads Gog.

decisions.choice: the remotest parts of the north

records.source: וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י קַשְׁתְּךָ֖ מִיַּ֣ד שְׂמֹאולֶ֑ךָ וְחִצֶּ֕יךָ מִיַּ֥ד יְמִינְךָ֖ אַפִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: And I will strike your bow from your left hand, and your arrows from your right hand I will make fall.
pieces: Then I will knock the bow from your left hand and make the arrows drop from your right hand.

L.3: And I will strike your bow out of your left hand, and I will make your arrows fall from your right hand.

R.3: Then I will knock your bow out of your left hand and make the arrows fall out of your right hand.

decisions.choice: bow in the left hand, arrows in the right
decisions.reason: An archer held the bow in his left hand and drew the arrow with his right. The LORD disarms Gog before he can shoot (compare Psalm 46:10; Hosea 1:5).

records.source: עַל־הָרֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל תִּפּ֗וֹל אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־אֲגַפֶּ֔יךָ וְעַמִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֑ךְ לְעֵ֨יט צִפּ֧וֹר כָּל־כָּנָ֛ף וְחַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה נְתַתִּ֥יךָ לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: On [the] mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples who [are] with you; to birds of prey, birds of every wing, and to the animals of the field I give you for food.
pieces: On Israel's mountains you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples with you. I will give you as food to birds of prey of every sort and to the wild animals.

L.4: Upon the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your bands and the peoples who [are] with you; to the birds of prey of every kind and to the beasts of the field I will give you for food.

R.4: You will die on the mountains of Israel, you and all your soldiers and the nations with you. I will let all kinds of birds and wild animals eat your bodies.

decisions.choice: birds of prey, birds of every wing: every kind of bird of prey
decisions.reason: The phrase "every wing" means every kind of bird (17:23). To be left as food for birds and animals was the worst of disgraces (29:5; Deuteronomy 28:26). Verses 17-20 return to the picture.

decisions.choice: You will die (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "fall" means here.

records.source: עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה תִּפּ֑וֹל כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: On [the] face of the field you will fall, for I have spoken, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: You will fall out in the open, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: You will fall on the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: You will die in the open country, because I have said so, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: for I have spoken: the LORD's word decides it
decisions.reason: The LORD's word is enough to bring it about (5:13, 15, 17; 17:21).

decisions.choice: declares (L, B) / says (R) the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The settled wording.

records.source: וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־אֵ֣שׁ בְּמָג֔וֹג וּבְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאִיִּ֖ים לָבֶ֑טַח וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety in the coastlands. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: And I will send fire upon Magog and upon those who live securely in the coastlands; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: I will send fire on Magog and on the people who feel safe in lands far away. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will send fire on Magog: Revelation 20:9
decisions.reason: Revelation 20:9 says that when Gog and Magog surround the camp of the saints, "fire came down from heaven and devoured them". Ezekiel speaks of fire on Magog's own land. The same words, "I will send fire on", open the judgments of Amos 1:4-2:5.

decisions.choice: the coastlands: distant lands across the sea
decisions.reason: The word *'iyyim* means islands and coastlands, the far-off lands of the Mediterranean (26:15, 18; 27:3). The judgment reaches to the ends of the earth. Those who "dwell securely" there are like Israel in 38:8, 11, but their safety does not save them.

decisions.choice: coastlands (L, B); lands far away (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'iyyim* in Isaiah. The refrain follows the settled wording.

records.source: וְאֶת־שֵׁ֨ם קָדְשִׁ֜י אוֹדִ֗יעַ בְּתוֹךְ֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹֽא־אַחֵ֥ל אֶת־שֵׁם־קָדְשִׁ֖י ע֑וֹד וְיָדְע֤וּ הַגּוֹיִם֙ כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קָד֖וֹשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And my holy name I will make known in [the] midst of my people Israel, and I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore; and the nations will know that I, Yahweh, [am the] Holy One in Israel.
pieces: Among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name known, and I will no longer let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name be profaned. Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am the Holy One in Israel.

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name I will make known in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; and never again will I let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name be profaned; and the nations will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Holy One in Israel.

R.7: I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel how holy {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is, and I will not let anyone disgrace {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name again. Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am the Holy One in Israel.

decisions.choice: the Holy One in Israel: Isaiah's title for the LORD
decisions.reason: Isaiah calls the LORD "the Holy One of Israel" (Isaiah 1:4; 12:6). Ezekiel says "the Holy One in Israel": the holy God is present among his people. The verse answers 36:20-23, where Israel's exile profaned his name.

decisions.choice: I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore
decisions.reason: Never again will the nations see Israel's ruin and think the LORD powerless (36:20).

decisions.choice: the Holy One (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The title follows Isaiah's settled wording. Literal follows the Hebrew order of the last clause ("I [am] the LORD, the Holy One in Israel"); Balanced and Readable say "I, the LORD, am the Holy One in Israel".

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה בָאָה֙ וְנִֽהְיָ֔תָה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה ה֥וּא הַיּ֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Look, it is coming, and it will be done, declares [the] Lord Yahweh. That [is] the day of which I have spoken.
pieces: It is coming! It will certainly take place, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. This is the day I have spoken of.

L.8: Look, it is coming, and it will be done, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. That [is] the day of which I have spoken.

R.8: It is coming, and it will surely happen, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. This is the day I told you about.

decisions.choice: that is the day of which I have spoken
decisions.reason: The day is the day of Gog's defeat, which the earlier prophets foretold (38:17). It is as sure as if it had already come (compare 7:6, 10).

records.source: וְֽיָצְא֞וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י׀עָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּבִעֲר֡וּ וְ֠הִשִּׂיקוּ בְּנֶ֨שֶׁק וּמָגֵ֤ן וְצִנָּה֙ בְּקֶ֣שֶׁת וּבְחִצִּ֔ים וּבְמַקֵּ֥ל יָ֖ד וּבְרֹ֑מַח וּבִעֲר֥וּ בָהֶ֛ם אֵ֖שׁ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] inhabitants of [the] cities of Israel will go out and make fires and burn the weapons, both shield and buckler, with bow and with arrows, and with war club and with spear; and they will make fires with them seven years.
pieces: Then the people living in the towns of Israel will go out and use the weapons for fuel, burning shields large and small, bows and arrows, war clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them to make fires.

L.9: And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and kindle fires and burn the weapons, shield and buckler, bow and arrows, war club and spear; and they will make fires with them for seven years.

R.9: Then the people living in the towns of Israel will go out and burn the enemy's weapons as firewood. They will burn shields, bows, arrows, clubs and spears. They will have enough to keep their fires burning for seven years.

decisions.choice: burning the weapons for seven years: the end of war
decisions.reason: The enemy's army was so vast that its weapons supply fuel for seven years, a number of completeness. Burning them means there will be no more war (Psalm 46:10; Isaiah 9:4; compare Isaiah 2:4).

decisions.choice: shield and buckler; war club: the arms of the army
decisions.reason: The *magen* was a small shield and the *tsinnah* a large one (38:4). The "staff of hand" is a club or javelin carried by foot soldiers.

decisions.choice: shields large and small (B); shields (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the two kinds of shield, Readable names them once.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יִשְׂא֨וּ עֵצִ֜ים מִן־הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְלֹ֤א יַחְטְבוּ֙ מִן־הַיְּעָרִ֔ים כִּ֥י בַנֶּ֖שֶׁק יְבַֽעֲרוּ־אֵ֑שׁ וְשָׁלְל֣וּ אֶת־שֹׁלְלֵיהֶ֗ם וּבָֽזְזוּ֙ אֶת־בֹּ֣זְזֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And they will not carry wood from the field nor cut [it] from the forests, for with the weapons they will make fires; and they will plunder those who plundered them and despoil those who despoiled them, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will burn the weapons for fuel. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: And they will not carry wood from the field or cut [any] from the forests, for they will make fires with the weapons; and they will plunder those who plundered them and despoil those who despoiled them, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: They will not have to gather wood from the fields or cut down trees in the forests, because they will burn the weapons instead. They will rob the people who robbed them and take things from those who took their things, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they will plunder those who plundered them: the reversal
decisions.reason: Gog came to take plunder (38:12-13); now Israel takes his. The same reversal is promised in Isaiah 33:1 and Zephaniah 2:9.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה בַיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא אֶתֵּ֣ן לְגוֹג֩׀מְקֽוֹם־שָׁ֨ם קֶ֜בֶר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל גֵּ֤י הָעֹֽבְרִים֙ קִדְמַ֣ת הַיָּ֔ם וְחֹסֶ֥מֶת הִ֖יא אֶת־הָעֹֽבְרִ֑ים וְקָ֣בְרוּ שָׁ֗ם אֶת־גּוֹג֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הֲמוֹנֹ֔הוְקָ֣רְא֔וּ גֵּ֖יא הֲמ֥וֹן גּֽוֹג׃
records.gloss: And it will be on that day: I will give to Gog a place there, a grave in Israel, the valley of the travelers east of the sea; and it will block the travelers; and there they will bury Gog and all his multitude, and they will call [it] the valley of Hamon-gog.
pieces: On that day I will give Gog a burial ground in Israel, the valley of the Travelers east of the sea, and it will block the way of those who travel through. There they will bury Gog and all his horde, and it will be called the valley of Hamon-gog.

L.11: And on that day I will give Gog a burial place there in Israel, the valley of the Travelers, east of the sea; and it will block the way of the travelers; and there they will bury Gog and all his horde, and they will call [it] the valley of Hamon-gog.

R.11: At that time I will give Gog a place in Israel where he will be buried. It is the valley of the Travelers, east of the Dead Sea. It will block the way for people traveling through. Gog and all his army will be buried there, and it will be called the valley of Hamon-gog, which means "Gog's army".

decisions.choice: the valley of the Travelers east of the sea: a place on the route east of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The sea is probably the Dead Sea. The valley may be one of the routes through the land of Moab, east of the Jordan. The word for "travelers" is close to the name of the mountains of Abarim in Moab (Numbers 27:12; 33:47-48), and some take it as that name, "the valley of Abarim". The exact place is unknown.

decisions.choice: Hamon-gog: "the horde of Gog"
decisions.reason: The name means "the multitude of Gog", from the word used for "all his multitude" just before it. Valleys were often named after what happened in them (Joshua 7:26; 2 Chronicles 20:26).

decisions.choice: it will block the travelers: the sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the mass of graves will block the road, or that the valley will be closed to travelers while the burying goes on. The Septuagint reads "they will close off the mouth of the valley". The Hebrew is kept, with its sense left open.

decisions.choice: the valley of the Travelers; Hamon-gog (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The valley's name is capitalized as a place name (m1). Hamon-gog is kept as a name at every level; Readable adds what it means, as the text plays on it. Readable names the Dead Sea for clarity.

records.heading: The burial of Gog's army

records.source: וּקְבָרוּם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְמַ֖עַן טַהֵ֣ר אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ שִׁבְעָ֖ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And the house of Israel will bury them, in order to cleanse the land, seven months.
pieces: The house of Israel will spend seven months burying them, to make the land clean.

L.12: And the house of Israel will be burying them for seven months, in order to cleanse the land.

R.12: It will take the people of Israel seven months to bury all the bodies and make the land clean again.

decisions.choice: burying the dead to cleanse the land
decisions.reason: Under the Law a dead body made a person and a place ritually unclean (Numbers 19:11-16), and a body left unburied defiled the land (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). The holy land must be cleansed of every corpse.

decisions.choice: seven months: a long and complete work
decisions.reason: The number shows the size of the enemy's army and the thoroughness of the cleansing.

records.source: וְקָֽבְרוּ֙ כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לְשֵׁ֑ם י֚וֹם הִכָּ֣בְדִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And all the people of the land will bury [them], and it will be to them for renown, the day I display my glory, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: All the people of the land will take part in the burying, and it will bring them honor on the day I display {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: And all the people of the land will do the burying, and it will be for them a [source of] renown, the day that I show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: All the people of the land will help bury them. People will honor them for it on the day I show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: it will be to them for renown: it will bring them honor
decisions.reason: The work of burying will bring the people a good name, or the day will be famous for them.

decisions.choice: the day I display my glory: the day the LORD shows himself
decisions.reason: The verb, from the root of "glory", means to show oneself glorious (28:22). The day of Gog's defeat is the day the LORD shows his glory.

records.source: וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י תָמִ֤יד יַבְדִּ֨ילוּ֙ עֹבְרִ֣ים בָּאָ֔רֶץ מְקַבְּרִ֣ים אֶת־הָעֹבְרִ֗ים אֶת־הַנּוֹתָרִ֛ים עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לְטַֽהֲרָ֑הּ מִקְצֵ֥ה שִׁבְעָֽה־חֳדָשִׁ֖ים יַחְקֹֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And men of continual [employment] they will set apart, passing through the land, burying, with those passing through, those remaining on the face of the land, to cleanse it; at the end of seven months they will search.
pieces: They will appoint men to work full time going through the land, and with them others to bury the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will begin a search.

L.14: And they will set apart men to work continually, passing through the land and burying, with those passing through, those [bodies] that remain on the surface of the land, to cleanse it; at the end of seven months they will make a search.

R.14: They will choose men whose only job will be to go through the land and bury the bodies still lying on the ground, so that the land will be clean. When the seven months are over, they will search the land again.

decisions.choice: passing through ... those passing through: the Hebrew is hard
decisions.reason: The verse uses the word "pass through" several times, and its parts are hard to fit together. It may describe two groups: men who go through the land looking for bones, and others who bury what they find (verse 15). The Septuagint does not have "those passing through".

decisions.choice: men of continuity: men employed full time
decisions.reason: The phrase means men with a continual task, set apart for this one work.

decisions.choice: [bodies] (L); the bodies (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say what "those that remain" are. Readable follows the reading with two groups (m1) only as far as the next verse makes plain.

records.source: וְעָבְר֤וּ הָעֹֽבְרִים֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְרָאָה֙ עֶ֣צֶם אָדָ֔ם וּבָנָ֥ה אֶצְל֖וֹ צִיּ֑וּן עַ֣ד קָבְר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ הַֽמְקַבְּרִ֔ים אֶל־גֵּ֖יא הֲמ֥וֹן גּֽוֹג׃
records.gloss: And the travelers will pass through the land, and [when] one sees a human bone, he will set up beside it a marker until the buriers bury it in the valley of Hamon-gog.
pieces: As they go through the land, whenever one of them sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it so that the gravediggers can bury it in the valley of Hamon-gog.

L.15: And as those passing through pass through the land and anyone sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it, until the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon-gog.

R.15: As these men go through the land, whenever one of them sees a human bone, he will put up a sign next to it. Then the gravediggers will come and bury it in the valley of Hamon-gog.

decisions.choice: a marker: a sign to warn of uncleanness and to show the buriers
decisions.reason: The marker, perhaps a pile of stones or a post, shows the buriers where the bone is and warns others not to touch it and become unclean (Numbers 19:16).

decisions.choice: a human bone (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *'adam* here means a human being, so each level says "human"; the one who sees it is one of the men appointed, so "he" needs no gender setting.

records.source: וְגַ֥ם שֶׁם־עִ֛יר הֲמוֹנָ֖ה וְטִהֲר֥וּ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: And also [the] name of [the] city [is] Hamonah; and they will cleanse the land.
pieces: A town there will also be named Hamonah. So they will cleanse the land.

L.16: And Hamonah will also be the name of a city. Thus they will cleanse the land.

R.16: There will also be a town named Hamonah, which means "Horde". In this way they will make the land clean.

decisions.choice: Hamonah: "horde", a town named after the event
decisions.reason: The name means "multitude" or "horde", like Hamon-gog in verse 11. No town of that name is known, and the words may be a note added to explain the burial site.

decisions.choice: which means "Horde" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name, which the text plays on (m1).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן־אָדָ֜ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אֱמֹר֩ לְצִפּ֨וֹר כָּל־כָּנָ֜ף וּלְכֹ֣ל׀חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה הִקָּבְצ֤וּ וָבֹ֨אוּ֙ הֵאָסְפ֣וּ מִסָּבִ֔יב עַל־זִבְחִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֜י זֹבֵ֤חַ לָכֶם֙ זֶ֣בַח גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וּשְׁתִ֥יתֶם דָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Say to birds of every wing and to every animal of the field: Assemble and come, gather from all around to my sacrifice that I am sacrificing for you, a great sacrifice on [the] mountains of Israel, and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
pieces: As for you, son of man, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Call out to every kind of bird and to all the wild animals: Assemble and come! Gather from all around to the sacrifice I am preparing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, where you will eat flesh and drink blood.

L.17: And you, son of man, thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Say to the birds of every kind and to every beast of the field, Assemble and come; gather from all around to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice that I am sacrificing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel; and you will eat flesh and drink blood.

R.17: Son of man, this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Call all the birds and wild animals. Tell them, Come together from all around to the great feast I am preparing for you on the mountains of Israel. I am offering it as a sacrifice. There you will eat meat and drink blood.

decisions.choice: my sacrifice: the slaughter of Gog's army pictured as a sacrificial feast
decisions.reason: A sacrifice was followed by a meal. Here the roles are reversed: the LORD prepares the meal, the guests are birds and wild animals, and the victims are the enemy soldiers (Isaiah 34:6; Jeremiah 46:10; Zephaniah 1:7). The picture is meant to shock.

decisions.choice: the birds called to the great feast: Revelation 19:17-18
decisions.reason: Revelation 19:17-18 takes up this picture: an angel calls to all the birds to gather for "the great supper of God", to eat the flesh of kings, commanders and horses.

decisions.choice: eat flesh and drink blood: a terrible reversal of the Law
decisions.reason: Israel was forbidden to eat blood (Leviticus 17:10-14), and the fat and blood of a sacrifice belonged to the LORD (Leviticus 3:16-17). The birds and beasts are invited to the feast forbidden to people.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Here the formula comes before the command to speak. The words the birds are to be told take no quotation marks, as a message Ezekiel delivers.

records.heading: The feast for the birds and beasts

records.source: בְּשַׂ֤ר גִּבּוֹרִים֙ תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ וְדַם־נְשִׂיאֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ תִּשְׁתּ֑וּ אֵילִ֨ים כָּרִ֤ים וְעַתּוּדִים֙ פָּרִ֔ים מְרִיאֵ֥י בָשָׁ֖ן כֻּלָּֽם׃
records.gloss: The flesh of warriors you will eat, and the blood of the princes of the earth you will drink: rams, lambs and goats, bulls, fatlings of Bashan all of them.
pieces: You will eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth as if they were rams and lambs, goats and bulls, all of them fattened animals from Bashan.

L.18: The flesh of warriors you will eat, and the blood of the princes of the earth you will drink: rams, lambs and goats, bulls, fatlings of Bashan all of them.

R.18: You will eat the bodies of soldiers and drink the blood of the world's rulers. They will be like rams, lambs, goats and bulls, all fattened animals from Bashan.

decisions.choice: rams, lambs, goats, bulls: the warriors pictured as sacrificial animals
decisions.reason: The leaders of the nations are pictured as the animals offered in sacrifice. Bashan, east of the Jordan, was famous for its rich pasture and fat cattle (Deuteronomy 32:14; Amos 4:1; Psalm 22:13).

decisions.choice: the princes of the earth: the rulers of the nations
decisions.reason: The word is *nasi'* (see 34:24), here of the rulers of the nations with Gog.

decisions.choice: as if they were (B); They will be like (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the comparison plain, which the Hebrew leaves to be understood. *Nasi'* of foreign rulers is "princes" at Literal and "rulers" at Balanced and Readable.

records.source: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם־חֵ֣לֶב לְשָׂבְעָ֔ה וּשְׁתִ֥יתֶם דָּ֖ם לְשִׁכָּר֑וֹן מִזִּבְחִ֖י אֲשֶׁר־זָבַ֥חְתִּי לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk from my sacrifice that I have sacrificed for you.
pieces: At the sacrifice I am preparing for you, you will eat fat till you are full and drink blood till you are drunk.

L.19: And you will eat fat to the full and drink blood to drunkenness, from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice that I am sacrificing for you.

R.19: At the sacrifice I am preparing for you, you will eat fat until you are stuffed and drink blood until you are drunk.

decisions.choice: fat and blood: the portions that belonged to God
decisions.reason: In Israel's sacrifices the fat and the blood were the LORD's and could not be eaten (Leviticus 3:16-17; 7:23-27). Here the LORD gives them to the birds and beasts.

decisions.choice: I am sacrificing (L); I am preparing (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is in the past tense, the sacrifice as good as done; each level says "am" to fit verse 17.

records.source: וּשְׂבַעְתֶּ֤ם עַל־שֻׁלְחָנִי֙ ס֣וּס וָרֶ֔כֶב גִּבּ֖וֹר וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will be satisfied at my table with horse and charioteer, with warrior and every man of war, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: At {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table you will be filled with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and every kind of soldier, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: And you will eat your fill at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table of horse and charioteer, of mighty men and all men of war, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: At {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} table you will eat all you want of horses and their riders, of strong soldiers and all kinds of fighting men, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: charioteer: the word means "chariot" or "rider"
decisions.reason: The word is usually "chariot", here perhaps "chariot team" or "chariot driver". With a small change it reads "rider", as in Revelation 19:18, "horses and their riders".

decisions.choice: my table: the LORD as host
decisions.reason: The LORD is the host of the feast (compare 44:16), and the guests are the birds and beasts.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־כְּבוֹדִ֖י בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָא֣וּ כָל־הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֶת־מִשְׁפָּטִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי וְאֶת־יָדִ֖י אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֥מְתִּי בָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see my judgment that I have executed and my hand that I have laid on them.
pieces: I will display {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory among the nations. Every nation will see the judgment I carry out and the power I use against them.

L.21: And I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory among the nations; and all the nations will see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment which I have carried out, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand which I have set on them.

R.21: I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory to the nations. All of them will see how I punish and how powerfully I act against them.

decisions.choice: I will set my glory among the nations: the passage turns to the meaning of it all
decisions.reason: Verses 21-29 sum up the purpose of chapters 38-39 and of the whole book: the nations will see the LORD's glory, Israel will know the LORD, and the nations will understand why Israel went into exile.

decisions.choice: my hand that I have laid on them: my power in judgment
decisions.reason: See 35:3. The hand is the LORD's power.

decisions.choice: the power I use (B); how powerfully I act (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "hand"; Balanced and Readable say what it stands for.

records.source: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה׃
records.gloss: And the house of Israel will know that I [am] Yahweh their God from that day and onward.
pieces: The house of Israel will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God from that day on.

L.22: And the house of Israel will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God from that day onward.

R.22: From then on the people of Israel will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: Israel will know that I am the LORD their God
decisions.reason: The refrain in its fullest form. From the time of the LORD's victory onward, Israel's knowledge of him will not fail again.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled, with "their God"
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain, with the subject named.

records.source: וְיָדְע֣וּ הַ֠גּוֹיִם כִּ֣י בַעֲוֺנָ֞ם גָּל֣וּ בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָֽעֲלוּ־בִ֔י וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם וָֽאֶתְּנֵם֙ בְּיַ֣ד צָרֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּפְּל֥וּ בַחֶ֖רֶב כֻּלָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And the nations will know that for their iniquity the house of Israel went into exile, because they acted unfaithfully against me; and I hid my face from them and gave them into [the] hand of their enemies, and they fell by [the] sword, all of them.
pieces: The nations will come to understand that the house of Israel was exiled because of its guilt, because it broke faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So I hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.

L.23: And the nations will know that for their iniquity the house of Israel went into exile, because they acted faithlessly against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them and I gave them into their foes' hand, and they fell by the sword, all of them.

R.23: And the nations will understand that the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners because of their sins. They were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I turned away from them. I let their enemies defeat them, and they were all killed in battle.

decisions.choice: for their iniquity Israel went into exile: not because the LORD was weak
decisions.reason: The nations had concluded that the LORD could not protect his people (36:20). Now they will understand that the exile was his judgment on Israel's sin.

decisions.choice: I hid my face from them: I withdrew my favor and protection
decisions.reason: To hide the face is to turn away, to withhold favor and help (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; Isaiah 54:8). Verse 29 promises that the LORD will never hide his face again.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully: broke faith
decisions.reason: The verb *ma'al* means to betray a trust owed to God (see 18:24).

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'awon*. Readable says "turned away from them" for the idiom (m2).

records.source: כְּטֻמְאָתָ֥ם וּכְפִשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם עָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹתָ֑ם וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them.
pieces: I dealt with them as their impurity and their rebellious acts deserved, and I hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them.

L.24: According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them.

R.24: I punished them because they were unclean and had sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I turned away from them.

decisions.choice: according to their uncleanness and transgressions: a just punishment
decisions.reason: The exile was in keeping with what they had done (36:19).

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellious acts (B); sinned (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *pesha'*.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עַתָּ֗ה אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְקִנֵּאתִ֖י לְשֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Now I will restore [the] fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on all [the] house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and show compassion to the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name.

L.25: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on all the house of Israel; and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name I will be jealous.

R.25: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Now I will make things good again for the descendants of Jacob. I will show mercy to all the people of Israel, and I will protect the honor of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy name.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes of Jacob: turn their lot around
decisions.reason: The phrase *shuv shevut* means to restore someone's fortunes, to reverse their condition (16:53; Jeremiah 30:3). The written Hebrew here can also be read "bring back the captivity", and both senses fit the return from exile.

decisions.choice: now: the book turns from the far future back to the exiles' present
decisions.reason: After the vision of the latter days (38:8, 16), "now" brings the promise back to the people Ezekiel is speaking to, in exile.

decisions.choice: I will be jealous for my holy name
decisions.reason: The LORD's jealousy, which burned against the nations that mocked his land (36:5-6), is his zeal for his own honor, and it moves him to have mercy on his people.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *shuv shevut* from Jeremiah. Readable says "the descendants of Jacob" for "Jacob" and "protect the honor of" for "be jealous for".

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will restore Israel

records.source: וְנָשׂוּ֙ אֶת־כְּלִמָּתָ֔ם וְאֶת־כָּל־מַעֲלָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעֲלוּ־בִ֑י בְּשִׁבְתָּ֧ם עַל־אַדְמָתָ֛ם לָבֶ֖טַח וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And they will bear their shame and all their unfaithfulness that they committed against me, when they dwell securely on their land with none to make [them] afraid,
pieces: They will bear their shame and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, when they live in safety in their own land with no one to frighten them,

L.26: And they will bear their disgrace and all their unfaithfulness that they committed against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, when they dwell securely on their own soil with no one to make [them] afraid,

R.26: They will be ashamed of how they were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even when they are living in safety in their own land with no one to frighten them.

decisions.choice: they will bear their shame: or "they will forget their shame"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read "they will bear" or, with one letter understood differently, "they will forget". On the first reading they will feel the shame of their past unfaithfulness when they are restored, as in 16:63 and 36:31-32; on the second, their shame will be over. The standard reading, "bear", is kept.

decisions.choice: dwelling securely with none to make them afraid: 34:28
decisions.reason: The promise of 34:25-28 and Leviticus 26:6.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 27, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

records.source: בְּשׁוֹבְבִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ מִן־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְקִבַּצְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֔ם מֵֽאַרְצ֖וֹת אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וְנִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי בָ֔ם לְעֵינֵ֖י הַגּוֹיִ֥ם רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: when I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, and show myself holy through them before [the] eyes of many nations.
pieces: when I have brought them home from the peoples and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, and shown {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy through them before many nations.

L.27: when I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy through them in the sight of many nations.

R.27: I will bring them back from the nations and gather them from the lands of their enemies. Through what I do for them I will show many nations that I am holy.

decisions.choice: I will show myself holy through them before many nations
decisions.reason: As in 36:23 and 38:16, 23, the LORD shows his holiness by what he does for and through his people.

records.source: וְיָדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם בְּהַגְלוֹתִ֤י אֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְכִנַּסְתִּ֖ים עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־אוֹתִ֥יר ע֛וֹד מֵהֶ֖ם שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh their God, in that I sent them into exile among the nations and gathered them to their land, and I will not leave any of them there again.
pieces: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them back into their own land, leaving none of them behind.

L.28: And they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, because I sent them into exile among the nations and have gathered them into their own land; and I will leave none of them there any longer.

R.28: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. I sent them away as prisoners among the nations, and I brought them all back to their own land. I did not leave any of them behind.

decisions.choice: I sent them into exile and gathered them: both are the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: The same God who judged them restores them. Exile and return together show who he is.

decisions.choice: I will not leave any of them there: missing in the Septuagint
decisions.reason: The Septuagint does not have the end of verse 28 and the first part of verse 29. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled, with "their God"
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־אַסְתִּ֥יר ע֛וֹד פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁפַ֤כְתִּי אֶת־רוּחִי֙ עַל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I will no longer hide my face from them, for I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Never again will I hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them, because I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.29: And I will no longer hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them, when I have poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.29: I will never turn away from them again, because I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on the people of Israel, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel: 36:27; 37:14; Joel 3:1
decisions.reason: The promise of the LORD's Spirit (36:27; 37:14) is now described as poured out like water, as in Joel 3:1-2, "I will pour out my Spirit on all people", and Isaiah 44:3. Peter quotes Joel at Pentecost (Acts 2:17-18).

decisions.choice: I have poured out: the gift seen as already done
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is in the past tense, but it describes the future; the promise is so certain that it is spoken of as done. It also explains why the LORD will never again hide his face.

decisions.choice: have poured out (L); will pour out (B, R); Spirit, capitalized
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew tense; Balanced and Readable give its future sense (m2). "Spirit" is capitalized as the LORD's Spirit, as at 2:2 and 36:27. Readable says "turn away from them" for hiding the face, as in verse 23.
